interactions.detail: The sample display name and `#<id>` render as plain nested <span>s with no onClick, no href, no role, and no keyboard focus. A scientist scanning the corpus will reach for the sample's NAME to open it — the single most obvious affordance on the row — and nothing happens. The only way into a sample is double-clicking a frame thumbnail (opens the loupe) which is undiscoverable, or via the footer legend. There is NO path at all from a row to the Index/focus workspace at /sample/:id (confirmed: the only navigate(`/sample/...`) call sites are the topbar stepper at CorpusTopbar.tsx:251,270, which only render once you are already on /sample/:id).
interactions.recommendation: Make the sample name a real link. Lowest-friction: name double-click-or-single-click opens the loupe (matching the thumb), and add a small explicit 'Index ->' affordance per row (or make the name the loupe link and surface an 'Open in Index' action in the loupe) so /sample/:id is reachable from the corpus. At minimum wrap the identity block in a <Link to={`/samples/loupe/${sample.id}`}> so the most-targeted element is not dead.

interactions.detail: Real <button>; onClick toggles the frame into the row-local selection set (shiftKey extends a contiguous range from the last-clicked anchor). Drives the floating CullBar and the X/Esc keystrokes. Works and is keyboard-focusable, but single-click-to-select competes with double-click-to-open (see below) and the function is non-obvious without reading the footer legend.
interactions.recommendation: Selection-by-clicking-an-image is a hidden affordance. Consider a visible per-frame select control on hover, or a row-level 'select all dropped/kept' helper, so culling does not depend on the user discovering that clicking the picture selects it.

interactions.detail: onDoubleClick -> navigate(`/samples/loupe/${sample.id}`). Works, but a double-click necessarily fires onClick (select) first, so opening the loupe leaves a frame selected and pops the CullBar for a beat. Double-click is the ONLY mouse path off the row into a sample, and it is undiscoverable without the footer legend. It also opens the loupe, never the Index workspace.
interactions.recommendation: Overloading one image target with click=select and dblclick=open is fragile and hidden. Promote sample-open to a discoverable target (the name, per missing-entry-point above), and reserve thumbnails for culling only — or have dblclick clear the transient single-frame select it triggered.

interactions.detail: Keydown Enter/Space preventDefaults and calls onOpenLoupe. So a keyboard user can OPEN a sample but has no keyboard analogue to SELECT a frame (the click handler is mouse-only via the synthesized-click suppression). Keyboard users therefore cannot reach the cull/drop flow at all — they can only open the loupe.
interactions.recommendation: Give keyboard users a select path (e.g. a modifier+Enter to toggle selection, or roving-tabindex with Space=select / Enter=open) so the X-drop workflow advertised in the footer legend is keyboard-reachable, not mouse-only.

interactions.element: Footer keyboard legend keycap chips (click / shift-click / X / double-click / Esc)
interactions.detail: The legend is the de-facto documentation for the row's hidden affordances. The X and Esc hints are conditionally live: the row-scoped keydown listener only mounts while a selection exists (ContactSheetRow.tsx:257-278). So 'X drop the selected frames' does nothing until you have first discovered the (hidden) click-to-select. The legend is always shown even when nothing is selected, advertising a key that is inert in the rest state. The chips themselves are non-interactive <span>s (display only).
interactions.recommendation: This sticky legend is carrying the entire discoverability burden for invisible interactions. Either make the affordances visible on the row (hover controls) so the legend becomes a reminder rather than the only documentation, or grey/disable the X & Esc chips until a selection exists to reflect their actual state.

interactions.detail: onReject -> handleBatchReject: for each selected, non-already-rejected exposure, fires setStatus.mutate({status:'rejected'}) (real queued mutation), then clears selection. Works. But it only ever REJECTS — there is no un-drop / restore on the contact sheet. Once dropped from here, the only un-reject path is opening the loupe (handleDropToggle there toggles back). One-way from the corpus view.
interactions.recommendation: Add an un-drop affordance reachable from the sheet (e.g. clicking an already-rejected frame offers Restore, or the CullBar offers Restore when the selection is all-rejected). The sheet is where bulk triage happens, so the inverse of a bulk drop belongs here, not only in the loupe.

interactions.detail: onClear -> clearSelection() empties the row-local selection set; Esc does the same via the row keydown listener. Works.
interactions.recommendation: No change.

interactions.detail: Opens the inline tag form (setTagFormOpen). Real button, keyboard-focusable. When chips exist it collapses to '+' and is opacity-0 until row hover OR focus-within (group-focus-within added for keyboard reach). When the row has zero tags it is the always-visible '+ tag' invite. The hover-only reveal when tags exist is a hidden affordance for mouse users not hovering, but keyboard reach is handled.
interactions.recommendation: The opacity-0-until-hover '+' is fine as a quiet affordance but is invisible on touch and easy to miss. Consider a low-contrast always-visible '+' so adding a second tag does not require discovering hover-reveal.

interactions.element: Inline tag form — value input (Enter submits / Esc cancels) + Add button
interactions.detail: autoFocus on the value input; Enter -> submitTag (trims value, requires non-empty, fires addTag.mutate via useAddCorpusSampleTag -> real queue mutator), Esc -> resetTagForm. The 'Add' button and explicit '×' cancel both work. Note: submit requires a non-empty VALUE but the KEY is optional, and the key input has no Enter/Esc handler (only the value input does) — focusing the key field and pressing Enter does nothing.
interactions.recommendation: Add the same onKeyDown (Enter/Esc) to the key input so the form submits from either field. Minor.

interactions.detail: aria-labelled 'Remove <key> tag'; onClick -> removeTag.mutate(t.id) via useRemoveCorpusSampleTag (real queue mutator). Works, keyboard-focusable. No confirm (acceptable for a light note). The chip body itself is not interactive — only the × removes — which is correct.
interactions.recommendation: No change.

interactions.detail: Pure <span> with a title ('screened' / 'not yet screened') and an SVG tick — no onClick, no role, not focusable. The screened state is DERIVED, not stored: isSampleScreened (lib/sample/screened.ts:19-26) returns the backend flag if present (not yet wired) else true only when every exposure has a non-null status. So a scientist cannot mark a sample screened/unscreened; it flips only as a side-effect of triaging every frame. The page header 'N / total samples screened' progress bar (SamplesPage.tsx:124-139) is driven entirely by this derived value and is likewise not directly actionable.
interactions.recommendation: If 'screened' is meant to be a user judgement (the copy says 'looked at and triaged'), make the dot a real toggle backed by the #162 flag. If it stays purely derived, give it a tooltip explaining it auto-fills when all frames are triaged, so the inert dot does not read as a broken checkbox.

interactions.element: Status cell — 'Not indexed' hollow dot / phase chip
interactions.detail: Renders SampleStatusChip(sample.phase). sample.phase is a forward-looking seam with no corpus-level indexing rollup wired, so every row reads 'Not indexed' with a hollow dot and no link. A scientist sees 'Not indexed' on every sample and would reasonably expect clicking it to start indexing — it is the natural CTA into the Index workspace. It is a non-interactive <span>. This is the second missing entry point into /sample/:id: the status column literally says the sample is not indexed but offers no way to index it.
interactions.recommendation: Make the 'Not indexed' affordance the click-to-index entry: link/button -> /sample/${id} (the Index workspace). This is the most intent-aligned place to add the missing corpus->Index path.

interactions.element: Loupe segment of the Contact sheet | Loupe view switch (topbar)
interactions.detail: On /samples the Loupe segment renders as a permanently disabled <button title='Open a sample to use the loupe'> (cursor-not-allowed). It only becomes the active <span> once you are ALREADY on /samples/loupe/:id (reached by double-clicking a frame). So the segmented control can never be used to GET to the loupe — it only reflects state after you arrive by another path. A user who reads 'Contact sheet | Loupe' will click Loupe expecting to open one, and get a dead, tooltip-only control.
interactions.recommendation: A view switch that cannot switch is friction. Either (a) make Loupe open the last-viewed / first sample's loupe, or (b) drop the Loupe segment from the sheet entirely and rely on row-level open affordances — the segment as-is is a permanent dead control on the primary corpus route.

interactions.detail: onChange writes/removes ?beamtime=<experiment_id> in the URL; SamplesPage reads it and filters the corpus client-side. Real <select>, keyboard-operable, options from useExperiments. Works. The title (SamplesPage.tsx:74-75) and the screened-progress aggregate both track the filter. One friction: it is the ONLY filter — no search/sort/tag filter over ~139 samples, so finding a specific sample in the corpus relies on scrolling.
interactions.recommendation: Works as a beamtime facet. Consider (separate scope) a text/tag filter given the ~139-sample corpus; not a wiring bug.

interactions.detail: <Link to='/samples'>, active via pathname prefix. Works. This is the current surface so it is the active tab.
interactions.recommendation: No change.

interactions.detail: The Index tab has no `to`; on /samples isActive is false so it renders disabled (cursor-not-allowed). It only un-disables as a non-navigable current-stage marker when already on /sample/:id (F-14). So from the corpus, the workflow stepper shows an 'Index' stage that the user cannot click to enter — reinforcing that there is no advertised way to get from the corpus into indexing. The IA promises a Samples -> Index -> Series flow but the middle step is unreachable from step one.
interactions.recommendation: The Index tab being permanently disabled on the corpus is the topbar symptom of the same missing entry point. Once row-level 'Not indexed'/name links into /sample/:id exist, consider making the Index tab navigate to the first un-indexed sample (or the active one) so the global workflow stepper is actually traversable left-to-right.

interactions.detail: <Link to='/series'>. Works, navigates off this surface to the Series folio. Out of scope for this surface but confirmed live.
interactions.recommendation: No change.

interactions.detail: Plain <span>, no link. Users conventionally expect a wordmark to be a home link. Minor — /samples is effectively home and the Samples tab covers it.
interactions.recommendation: Optional: make the wordmark a Link to '/'. Low priority.

interactions.detail: Inner canvas is role='img' aria-label='Detector image', not itself interactive — interaction lives on the wrapping <button> in ExposureThumb (correct). Thumbs lazy-load via IntersectionObserver (200px rootMargin) to avoid the 139x fan-out. While off-screen / pre-decode the row shows 'Loading frames…' / placeholder. No interactive defect.
interactions.recommendation: No change.

frictionFindings: The single highest-friction issue: from the corpus there is NO discoverable path into a sample. The name, #id, screened-mark, and status cell are all inert; the only mouse path is double-clicking a frame image (hidden, documented only in the footer legend) and it lands in the loupe, never the Index workspace. The scientist's primary intent — 'open this sample / index this sample' — costs an undiscoverable double-click or nothing at all.

Two natural CTAs are wasted: the sample name (most-targeted element) and the 'Not indexed' status chip (literally invites indexing) are both non-interactive. Wiring either to /samples/loupe/:id or /sample/:id removes the dead-end with near-zero new UI.

Hidden-affordance overload: click=select, dblclick=open-loupe, and shift-click=range are all stacked on the same frame image with no visible affordance. The sticky footer legend is the ONLY documentation; remove the legend and the row becomes inscrutable.

Keyboard users can open a sample (Enter/Space on a thumb) but cannot select frames or use the advertised X-drop flow at all — the select handler is mouse-only. The footer legend advertises X but it is inert for keyboard and inert in the rest state for everyone.
Culling is one-way from the sheet: the CullBar only Drops, never Restores. Un-rejecting requires opening the loupe. The bulk-triage surface lacks the inverse of its bulk action.

The Loupe view-switch segment is a permanent dead control on /samples (disabled, tooltip-only) — a 'switch' that cannot initiate the switch. Same for the Index stage tab, which is disabled on the corpus, so the Samples->Index->Series workflow stepper is not traversable from step one.
The screened-mark looks like a checkbox (dot + tick) but is inert and purely derived; it reads as a broken toggle. The header progress bar is likewise non-actionable.
Tag form: only the value input has Enter/Esc; the key input does not, so submitting from the key field silently fails.
No way to find a specific sample in a ~139-row corpus other than the beamtime select + scrolling — no text/tag search or sort.
deadEnds: The Index/focus workspace at /sample/:id is unreachable from the contact sheet. Grep confirms the only navigate(`/sample/:id`) call sites are the topbar stepper (CorpusTopbar.tsx:251,270), which renders ONLY when already on /sample/:id. There is no first entry into the Index stage from the corpus — the workflow's middle step has no front door from its first step.

The loupe (/samples/loupe/:id) is itself a dead-end with respect to indexing: LoupeSidebar.tsx:311 says 'One exposure per sample carries forward to the Index stage' but provides no link to /sample/:id. So even after the hidden double-click into the loupe, there is no onward path to indexing — only navigate('/samples') back (LoupePage.tsx:137).

Loupe view-switch segment (CorpusTopbar.tsx:226-234): permanently disabled on /samples; it can reflect the loupe state but can never be used to enter the loupe — a control with no reachable active path from this route.

Index stage tab (CorpusTopbar.tsx:139-161): disabled on the corpus with no navigation target; a visible workflow step that is a no-op until you arrive at /sample/:id by some other (nonexistent-from-here) means.

Screened-mark (ContactSheetRow.tsx:323-346) and screened-progress (SamplesPage.tsx:124-139): a state surfaced as if interactive but with no control to set it — the only way to flip 'screened' is to triage every frame's status.
notes: All handlers were traced to live code. Tag add/remove and exposure-status mutations route through real queue mutators (useAddCorpusSampleTag/useRemoveCorpusSampleTag/useSetExposureStatus in queries.ts:579-602) — those flows are genuinely wired and work. The defects on this surface are not broken wiring but missing/hidden entry points and overloaded affordances. The KNOWN items from the brief are all confirmed: sample identity is inert <span>s (ContactSheetRow.tsx:347-354); the Loupe topbar segment is permanently disabled on /samples (CorpusTopbar.tsx:226-234); the only interactive per-row elements are the frame thumbnails and the +tag flow. The most consequential finding beyond the brief: the loupe does not link onward to the Index workspace either, so /sample/:id has no front door anywhere in the corpus->loupe path — the single change with the highest leverage is making the 'Not indexed' status chip and/or the sample name link into a sample-detail route. Routing verified in components/AppRoutes.tsx (lines 88-91): /samples, /samples/loupe/:sampleId (LoupePage), and /sample/:sampleId (FocusWorkspacePage, the Index surface) are three distinct routes."

surface: Focus workspace (/sample/:sampleId) — trace plate (PlotCard/TraceViewer), phase-call rail (IndicesCard/PhasePanel), co-resident detector (FocusDetectorPanel/DetectorRingOverlay), reflections table (FocusReflectionsTable), notes margin/drawer (FocusNotesMargin), and the surface's topbar affordances in CorpusTopbar (sample stepper + Notes toggle).

interactions.element: Candidate row (whole row click = toggle membership in active phase call)
interactions.detail: role=checkbox, tabIndex=0, Enter/Space handled (114-116), onClick=onToggle → toggle(ix) which calls addMember.mutate / removeMember.mutate against the active group. There is NO separate 'Fit' or 'Confirm' button on the rail — toggling the checkbox IS the curation and it persists immediately via the mutation queue. The owner's 'Fit / Confirm/curate' mental model does not map to any rail control; the only commit gesture is the inline toggle.
interactions.recommendation: Keep the inline-toggle-as-commit model (it is low-friction). But the rail header 'Index choices' + the buried explanatory paragraph never tell the user that a click commits — add one quiet line of affordance copy ('click to add/remove from the call; saved instantly') so the absence of a Confirm button is intentional-feeling rather than a missing step.

interactions.detail: Row IS keyboard-operable (tabIndex=0 + Enter/Space) and onFocus/onBlur drive the same hover-preview as mouse (119-120). BUT there is no focus-visible ring class anywhere on the row — only border/background tint changes on inCall state. A keyboard user tabbing through candidates gets NO visible focus indicator, so the row is reachable but invisibly so (the KNOWN issue from the brief, confirmed in source).
interactions.recommendation: Add a focus-visible outline (outline-2 outline-accent, matching plot-title at PlotCard.tsx:451) to the candidate row. The handlers are already correct; only the visible-focus token is missing.

interactions.element: Speculative delete (trash button on speculative candidate rows)
interactions.detail: Only rendered for speculative indices (onDelete passed at 377). stopPropagation prevents the row toggle, calls deleteIndex.mutate. Emoji glyph 🗑 as the only label — no SVG icon, off-brand for 'The Print' ink/paper system, and it is the single emoji in the rail.
interactions.recommendation: Replace the 🗑 emoji with an ink-stroke trash SVG consistent with the rest of the design system.

interactions.element: + Add speculative (dashed CTA inside the Speculative <details>)
interactions.detail: Opens the SpeculativeBuilder modal via openBuilder(exposureId). The CTA lives INSIDE a native <details> that is collapsed by default (open only when speculatives already exist, line 361). So the primary entry point to hand-build an index for a sparse pattern is hidden behind a disclosure a first-time user must discover and expand. For the structural scientist whose whole job on a sparse pattern is to hypothesize a phase, the main tool is one undiscoverable click away.
interactions.recommendation: Surface the '+ Add speculative' affordance (or at least the disclosure summary in an inviting state) whenever the phase call is empty / coverage is low — that is exactly when the user needs it. Tying its visibility to 'speculatives already exist' inverts the need.

interactions.detail: Native <details>/<summary> with list-none; keyboard-operable via the browser default. RailHead inside has no caret/chevron affordance, so it does not read as expandable — looks like a static section label.
interactions.recommendation: Add a disclosure chevron to the summary so it reads as expandable.

interactions.element: SpeculativeBuilder = the actual 'Fit' surface (phase select, anchor peak, anchor ratio, ratio-position checkboxes, Save)
interactions.detail: Full modal: phase <select>, anchor-peak <select>, anchor-ratio number input, per-ratio-position include checkboxes, Save (disabled until anchor set / while pending), Cancel, Esc-to-close, scrim-click-to-close, focus trap. This is the closest thing on the surface to the owner's 'Fit'. It is a modal where the rail has plenty of vertical room — an inline rail expansion would be lower-friction and keep the trace/predicted-q ticks visible while the user tunes the anchor (currently the modal covers the plate).
interactions.recommendation: Consider rendering the builder inline in the rail (or as a non-modal side sheet) so the user can watch predicted-q ticks update on the trace as they change phase/anchor, instead of a modal that occludes the very plot they are fitting against.

interactions.element: Trace empty-area click → add manual peak
interactions.detail: Click on empty plot interior calls xScale.invert(clickX) and onAddPeak(q) → addPeak.mutate. Works regardless of the '+ Peak' armed state (the armed toggle is purely presentational, see next row). There is NO on-canvas hint that a click adds a peak; the only affordance is the '+ Peak' button's tooltip 'Click the trace to place a peak'. Add-peak is therefore a hidden gesture for anyone who doesn't hover the button.
interactions.recommendation: When '+ Peak' is armed, change the trace cursor to crosshair and/or show a one-line inline hint over the plot. Right now arming changes only the button color (PlotCard.tsx:507-509) and a data-attr — the trace itself gives no feedback that click=add.

interactions.element: '+ Peak' tool button (arm 'place a peak' mode)
interactions.detail: aria-pressed + colored armed state work, but the armed flag does NOTHING functional: TraceViewer adds a peak on ANY empty-area click whether armed or not (handleClick has no addArmed guard, TraceViewer.tsx:264-291). The code comments explicitly call it 'Presentational only' (PlotCard.tsx:112-114, TraceViewer.tsx:39-41). So a user who clicks '+ Peak' expecting to enter a mode, then clicks a peak triangle, will instead toggle/remove that peak — the button promised a mode it does not enforce.
interactions.recommendation: Either make armed mode real (while armed, every interior click adds a peak and suppresses the remove/exclude branch; disarm after placing, or stay armed until toggled off), or remove the button and rely purely on click-to-add. A toggle whose state has no behavioral effect is a trap.

interactions.element: Trace peak triangle click → remove (manual) or toggle-exclude (auto)
interactions.detail: nearestClickablePeak within 10px: manual peak → onRemovePeak; auto peak → onTogglePeakExclusion (toggles excluded). Same single click does three different things (add / remove / exclude) depending on what's under the cursor and the peak's source. Powerful but entirely undiscoverable and overloaded — no labels, no right-click menu, no hover tooltip on the triangle saying what a click will do. A scientist cannot tell that clicking an auto peak excludes it vs clicking a manual peak deletes it.
interactions.recommendation: Disambiguate: hover a triangle should show a tooltip ('click to exclude' / 'click to delete') and/or the peak should have an explicit small affordance. At minimum document the gesture in the legend. The overloaded single-click is the core of the 'plot components need redesign' note.

interactions.detail: Peaks with id<0 are skipped by nearestClickablePeak (deliberate, to avoid the ghost-peak desync) and render as outlined triangles. Correct and intentional; the outline is the (subtle) signal that it is not yet clickable.
interactions.recommendation: None — this is a well-reasoned guard. Optionally make the outlined state slightly more distinct (e.g. dashed) so the 'not yet' reads at a glance.

interactions.detail: Wheel over the plot zooms x-domain around the cursor (log- or linear-aware), preventDefault on a non-passive listener. No on-canvas hint that wheel zooms; discoverable only by trying. No pinch/touch path and no keyboard zoom.
interactions.recommendation: Add a faint affordance (the ZoomIndicator already appears once zoomed; consider a one-time hint, or rely on Auto-fit). Acceptable for a power tool but undiscoverable for first use.

interactions.detail: dblclick calls onReset → resetDomain (clears x and y domain). Undiscoverable (no hint); overlaps with the ZoomIndicator 'reset' and Auto-fit affordances which DON'T do the same thing — dblclick clears to full range, while ZoomIndicator/Auto-fit re-FIT to features (PlotCard.tsx:480, 201-206). Two different 'reset' behaviors with no labeling of the difference.
interactions.recommendation: Reconcile the two resets. 'reset' on the ZoomIndicator (PlotCard.tsx:480 onReset=onFitFeatures) actually auto-FITS rather than resetting to full range — the label 'zoomed · reset' is misleading. Either make it truly reset (full q-range, matching dblclick) or relabel it 'fit'.

interactions.detail: Only rendered when xDomain!==null. onClick=onFitFeatures (NOT resetDomain) — so the control labeled 'reset' actually re-fits to features. Functional but the verb is wrong.
interactions.recommendation: Relabel to 'fit' or wire it to resetDomain to match the label.

interactions.detail: Computes a feature-focused x/y domain and applies it. disabled when !canFit (traceQ.data undefined). Clear label, good tooltip. This is the closest thing to the owner's 'Fit' on the plot side.
interactions.recommendation: None.

interactions.detail: Two buttons in a segmented control, data-active reflects state, onClick sets xType. Works and persists per-session. No focus-visible styling distinct from hover, but reachable.
interactions.recommendation: Add a focus-visible ring for keyboard parity (minor).

interactions.detail: disabled gated on !traceQ.data || !peaksQ.data (exportDisabled). Wired via exportSpec callback. Not read in detail here (separate component) but the gate is correct.
interactions.recommendation: None for this sweep.

interactions.detail: On the focus surface the header is a static FocusPlotHeader (sample name / code / beamtime / exposure). The legacy clickable 'plot-title' button (onClick→openNavModal, the experiment/sample picker) is DROPPED in the focus variant (442: headerSlot ?? button). So the title that on the Index page is a picker is here a non-interactive label. That is intentional (route seeds the sample), but it removes the in-context way to jump to a different sample from the title — the user must use the topbar stepper or the global nav modal.
interactions.recommendation: Intentional and defensible. Ensure the header doesn't LOOK clickable (no hover affordance) so users don't try to click it expecting the picker.

interactions.element: Reflections table row hover → q-link cross-highlight
interactions.detail: onMouseEnter sets hoveredQ=peak.q; guarded onMouseLeave clears only if still the active q. Drives the trace triangle halo + detector ring highlight (the q-link triple). data-hot tints the row. Works well via mouse.
interactions.recommendation: None for mouse.

interactions.detail: The <tr> has cursor-pointer and mouse handlers but NO tabIndex, NO key handler, NO onFocus/onBlur. A keyboard user cannot reach a reflection row at all, so the q-link cross-highlight is mouse-only. The cursor-pointer styling also implies the row is clickable, but onClick does nothing — only hover does (KNOWN issue, confirmed).
interactions.recommendation: Either (a) add tabIndex=0 + onFocus/onBlur mirroring the mouse handlers (matching CandidateRow's pattern) so q-link is keyboard-accessible, or (b) drop cursor-pointer since there is no click action — the pointer cursor falsely promises a click.

interactions.detail: Row has cursor-pointer (151) signaling clickability but there is no onClick — clicking a reflection row does nothing. A scientist would reasonably expect clicking a reflection to e.g. select/zoom that peak on the trace or toggle its inclusion.
interactions.recommendation: Give the row click a job (scroll/zoom the trace to that q, or toggle exclude), or remove cursor-pointer. An inert pointer cursor is a dead affordance.

interactions.detail: Wide transparent hit-ring (strokeWidth 5, pointerEvents:stroke) sets hoveredQ on enter, guarded clear on leave. Mouse-only (SVG, aria-hidden, no keyboard path). Works as the third leg of the q-link triple.
interactions.recommendation: Mouse-only is acceptable for a presentational overlay; the table/trace are the primary surfaces.

interactions.detail: Only rendered when exposures.length>1 (showSwitcher). onClick=setActiveExposure(e.id) — switches the VIEWED exposure (local view state, not persisted). ring-2 ring-print-accent marks viewed; a dot marks the persisted representative. Reachable, labeled via title. Good.
interactions.recommendation: None.

interactions.detail: disabled when viewedIsRep || exposure===undefined; persists the viewed exposure as representative via setRepresentative.mutate. When the viewed exposure IS the rep the button shows 'Representative' and is disabled (correct dead-end state, not an error). Only appears in the switcher (length>1).
interactions.recommendation: None — disabled-when-already-rep is the right affordance.

interactions.element: Notes textarea (margin, xl+) — focus-gated edit + save on blur
interactions.detail: Save happens ONLY on blur (onBlur → onSaveNotes(draft)). No explicit Save button, no Cmd+Enter, no autosave-on-pause. If the user types a note and navigates away via the stepper/keyboard without blurring the textarea first, the edit MAY be lost (blur normally fires on unmount-driven focus loss, but this is fragile — there is no visible 'saved' confirmation either). Also: the save-on-blur model gives zero feedback that the note persisted.
interactions.recommendation: Add a subtle 'saved' indicator (or a Save affordance) and consider Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to commit. The silent blur-only save with no confirmation is low-trust for a scientist recording observations.

interactions.element: Notes drawer (< xl) + scrim + close button
interactions.detail: role=dialog, scrim click closes (139), × close button closes (150-158). BUT there is NO focus trap and NO Esc-to-close on this drawer (compare SpeculativeBuilder which has both). A keyboard user opening the drawer can tab out behind the scrim, and Esc does nothing.
interactions.recommendation: Add useFocusTrap + Esc-to-close to the notes drawer, matching SpeculativeBuilder.tsx:39,100-104. As a role=dialog it should trap focus and respond to Esc.

interactions.detail: xl:hidden; onClick=toggleNotesDrawer; has-notes dot badge. Only entry point to notes below xl. Reachable, labeled. Works.
interactions.recommendation: None.

interactions.detail: navigate(`/sample/${id}`) on click; disabled at ends; aria-labels present. Siblings scoped to the active sample's experiment via corpusSamples. This is the working primary inter-sample nav on the focus surface — correctly URL-routed.
interactions.recommendation: None. This is the affordance that actually works for stepping.

interactions.element: ',' / '.' keyboard shortcut (prev/next sample) on the focus surface
interactions.detail: TWO independent reasons it's dead on /sample/:id: (1) useGlobalShortcuts receives samples gated on activeExperimentId!==undefined (AppRoutes.tsx:79), but the focus route seeds only activeSampleId, never activeExperimentId (useSyncActiveSampleFromRoute + setActiveSample cascade clears it) — so samplesQuery is disabled and the handler gets undefined → early return. (2) Even if seeded, the handler calls setActiveSample(next.id) (store-only) while the focus surface is URL-driven with a ONE-WAY URL→store sync — so the store change would not update the route and would be reverted on the next route re-sync. The OnboardingFlow still tells users 'Press , and . to jump to the previous or next sample' (OnboardingFlow.tsx:37), so the app advertises a shortcut that is inert here.
interactions.recommendation: On the focus surface, make ',' / '.' call navigate(`/sample/${prev/next.id}`) using the SAME experiment-scoped siblings the topbar stepper already computes (CorpusTopbar.tsx:64-72), instead of setActiveSample. Either centralize the stepper's prev/next derivation and bind the shortcut to it, or have the shortcut detect the /sample/ route and navigate. As-is the documented keyboard nav does nothing on the workspace it's documented for.

interactions.detail: Appears only when indices' inputs_hash != exposure.analysis_inputs_hash (after debounce, and hidden during pending peak ops). onClick=reanalyze.mutate({}); shows 'Re-analyzing…' while pending. Correct conditional surface — the re-fit entry point after peak curation.
interactions.recommendation: None. This is the well-designed 'your edits changed the inputs, refit' path.

interactions.element: Phase-call block (output cards in the rail)
interactions.detail: PhaseCallBlock is purely presentational — phase name, score, lattice, score bar, series ratio. No hover, no click, no link. A scientist might reasonably expect clicking a phase-call block to highlight that phase's predicted-q ticks on the trace (the candidate rows DO this on hover via setHoveredIndex, but the OUTPUT blocks do not). So the 'result' cards are inert while the 'input' candidate rows are interactive — an asymmetry.
interactions.recommendation: Wire phase-call block hover to setHoveredIndex (same as CandidateRow) so hovering a confirmed phase lights its ticks on the trace. Currently the user must scroll back down to the candidate row to preview the very phase that's in the call.

interactions.detail: The 'Index' tab has no `to`; on /sample/:id it is the active (non-navigable) current-stage marker (disabled={!isActive} → enabled-looking but cursor-default). Off a sample route it is inert/cursor-not-allowed. On the focus surface it's effectively a label, which is correct.
interactions.recommendation: None — intentional current-stage marker.

interactions.detail: Writes ?beamtime= to the URL, which the /samples sheet filters on. On the focus surface (/sample/:id) it still renders but has no effect on the current view — the focus surface doesn't read ?beamtime. So on this surface it's an expected-but-inert global control (changing it does nothing visible until you go to /samples).
interactions.recommendation: Minor: consider hiding or disabling the beamtime chip on /sample/:id where it has no local effect, to avoid a control that appears to do nothing on this surface.

frictionFindings: Peak editing on the trace is the central task and is entirely gesture-based with no labels: click-empty=add, click-manual=delete, click-auto=exclude, wheel=zoom, dblclick=reset. None of these are discoverable from the UI; only the '+ Peak' button has a tooltip, and that button doesn't even gate behavior. This is the heart of the owner's 'plot components need redesign'.

The '+ Peak' toggle is a false mode: it changes color/aria-pressed but the add-peak click works identically whether armed or not, and an armed user clicking a peak triangle will remove/exclude it instead of adding. A toggle with no behavioral effect actively misleads.

Two different 'reset' verbs on the plate that do different things: trace dblclick resets to FULL q-range; the 'zoomed · reset' link and Auto-fit re-FIT to features. The 'reset' label on the ZoomIndicator is wrong (it calls onFitFeatures).

The documented ',' / '.' sample-step shortcut is dead on the very surface (/sample/:id) where OnboardingFlow tells users to use it — gated on an experiment id the route never seeds, and even ungated would mutate store against a one-way URL→store sync.

The primary entry point to hand-build an index for a sparse pattern ('+ Add speculative') is hidden inside a collapsed <details> that only auto-opens once speculatives already exist — inverted from when the user needs it (empty/low-coverage phase call).

The phase-call OUTPUT blocks are inert while the candidate INPUT rows are hover-interactive; hovering a confirmed phase to preview its ticks requires scrolling back to the candidate, an asymmetry that adds clicks/scrolling.
Notes save silently on blur with no confirmation and no Save/Cmd-Enter affordance; risk of perceived data loss and zero trust feedback for a scientist recording observations.
Reflection rows carry cursor-pointer but have no onClick and no keyboard path — a dead pointer affordance and a mouse-only q-link.
Keyboard users get no focus-visible indicator on candidate rows (reachable but invisibly), and reflection rows aren't reachable at all — the q-link triple is mouse-only.
The Notes drawer (< xl) is a role=dialog with no focus trap and no Esc-to-close, unlike the SpeculativeBuilder modal which has both — inconsistent dialog behavior.
deadEnds: ',' / '.' keyboard shortcut on /sample/:id: handler runs but receives undefined samples (experiment id not seeded) and even when it would fire it sets store state that the one-way route sync reverts — the keystroke leads nowhere (useGlobalShortcuts.ts:48-61 + AppRoutes.tsx:79 + useSyncActiveSampleFromRoute.ts:13-17).

'+ Peak' armed mode: arming has no functional state to exit to — the mode doesn't change what a click does, so the user is in a 'mode' that isn't a mode (PlotCard.tsx:498-513 / TraceViewer.tsx:264-291).
Reflection row click: cursor-pointer invites a click that does nothing (FocusReflectionsTable.tsx:142-166).

Phase-call output block: looks like the result you'd interact with to inspect a confirmed phase, but it has no hover/click — to preview its ticks you must go back to the candidate row (PhasePanel.tsx:35-72).
Beamtime chip on /sample/:id: changing it has no visible effect on the focus surface (only affects /samples), a control that leads nowhere from here (CorpusTopbar.tsx:165-179).
notes:
Surface confirmed at FocusWorkspacePage → FocusWorkspaceLayout (grid: trace plate + lower [detector | reflections] | rail | notes). The owner's 'phase-call rail: candidate multi-select, Fit, Confirm/curate' does NOT map to discrete buttons: there is NO Fit and NO Confirm on the rail. Curation = clicking a candidate checkbox row, which immediately mutates the active group (PhasePanel.tsx:260-264) — commit is implicit. The 'Fit' a user would expect lives in two other places: trace Auto-fit (zoom, PlotCard.tsx:201-206) and the SpeculativeBuilder modal (hand-fit a phase). The re-fit-after-curation path is the StaleIndicesBanner 'Re-analyze' button.

The two highest-value wiring bugs to fix on this surface: (1) the dead ',' / '.' shortcut (documented in onboarding, inert here) and (2) the no-op '+ Peak' armed mode. The biggest redesign target (matching the owner's note) is the overloaded, unlabeled single-click peak-editing gesture set on the trace.

Keyboard reachability summary: CandidateRow = reachable but no focus-visible ring; ReflectionRow = not reachable at all (no tabIndex), cursor-pointer is a lie; SpeculativeBuilder modal = fully accessible (focus trap + Esc); Notes drawer = role=dialog but NO focus trap / NO Esc (inconsistent). Detector rings = mouse-only by design (presentational overlay)."

surface: Loupe — /samples/loupe/:sampleId (LoupePage + LoupeFrame + LoupeSidebar + DetectorImage + ThumbnailGallery, view-switch in CorpusTopbar)

interactions.detail: onClick=goBack -> navigate('/samples'). The ?beamtime= filter is NOT preserved (unlike CorpusTopbar's sheet link which appends beamtimeQuery), so a user who came from a filtered contact sheet lands back on the unfiltered all-experiments sheet. Also reachable via Esc key (LoupePage.tsx:150).
interactions.recommendation: Preserve the ?beamtime= query when navigating back, mirroring CorpusTopbar sheetHref (CorpusTopbar.tsx:196-197), so the user returns to the same filtered sheet they left.

interactions.detail: The h2 headline renders sample.display_name and the subtitle renders sample.name, both as plain static text. The task brief expects a tag/rename UI on the loupe. A rename pathway fully exists in the codebase: api.updateSample accepts {display_name} (api.ts:125) and useUpdateSample is wired (queries.ts:523), but it is only ever used for notes in FocusWorkspaceLayout (FocusWorkspaceLayout.tsx:88,126,162) — never for renaming, and never from the loupe. There is no rename affordance anywhere in the app.
interactions.recommendation: Make the loupe headline an inline-editable field (click-to-rename, Enter to commit) wired to useUpdateSample({display_name}). The single-sample loupe is the natural home for rename, and the backend + mutator already support it — only the UI affordance is missing.

interactions.detail: The only navigate() call in the entire Loupe surface is goBack -> '/samples' (LoupePage.tsx:137). There is NO link, button, or keyboard shortcut that takes the user from the loupe to the Focus/Index workspace at /sample/:id (route exists at AppRoutes.tsx:91). The sidebar even tells the user 'One exposure per sample carries forward to the Index stage' (LoupeSidebar.tsx:311-312) and offers 'Set as representative' — but after setting the rep there is no way to proceed TO indexing from here. The topbar Index tab is inert off a sample route (CorpusTopbar.tsx:140-160, disabled when !isActive), so it cannot bridge either. The user must go Back to the sheet, then re-find and open the sample in Focus by another route. This is the single biggest friction on the surface for the scientist whose intent is 'inspect, pick the frame, then index it'.
interactions.recommendation: Add a primary 'Index this sample' / 'Open in Focus' action on the loupe (e.g. in the Representative section, enabled once a representative exists) that navigates to /sample/:sampleId. This closes the inspect->index loop without a round-trip through the contact sheet.

interactions.detail: onClick=onSetRepresentative -> handleSetRepresentative -> setRepresentative.mutate(activeExposure.id) via useSelectExposure (LoupePage.tsx:120-123, queries.ts:604). Also bound to R/r key (LoupePage.tsx:149). On success the section swaps to the 'Representative for indexing' confirmation state (LoupeSidebar.tsx:303-307) driven by exposure.selected. No pending/disabled state while the queue mutation is in flight (useSelectExposure exposes isPending but it is not consumed), so a double-tap can fire two mutations; the queue idempotency key absorbs it but there is no visual in-flight feedback.
interactions.recommendation: Disable the button / show a brief in-flight state while setRepresentative.isPending to give immediate feedback and prevent double-fire. Consider pairing with the missing 'Open in Focus' action so 'set rep -> index' is one continuous flow.

interactions.detail: onClick=onDropToggle -> handleDropToggle -> setStatus.mutate({exposureId, status: rejected? null : 'rejected'}) (LoupePage.tsx:112-118). Also bound to X/x key (LoupePage.tsx:148); the mono 'X' keycap on the button surfaces the shortcut (LoupeSidebar.tsx:284-289). On drop the verdict label flips to 'Dropped', the dot goes terracotta, and the big frame gets the grease-pencil X + 'Dropped' badge (LoupeFrame.tsx:51-60). No in-flight disabled state (same as rep button).
interactions.recommendation: Optional: reflect setStatus.isPending with a brief disabled/spinner state for feedback parity with other queue mutations.

interactions.detail: Each cell has onClick={() => onSelect(e.id)} -> onSelectExposure -> setActiveId (LoupeFrame.tsx:70, LoupePage.tsx:218). Switching is also possible via Left/Right arrows (LoupePage.tsx:146-147, flip()). Selected cell gets a terracotta ring; rejected cells are dimmed+grayscaled; the indexing rep cell shows an '⊙ Indexing' badge.
interactions.recommendation: None for the switch itself. Affordance gap: the cell is a div with onClick and cursor-pointer but is NOT keyboard-focusable (no tabIndex/role/onKeyDown), unlike the contact-sheet thumb which is a real <button> with Enter/Space handling (ContactSheetRow.tsx:84-103). Arrow keys cover frame-flipping, but the strip itself is not tab-reachable. Make cells role=button + tabIndex=0 or render as <button> for AT parity.

interactions.detail: The big frame is a static canvas (role=img, aria-label 'Detector image'). There is NO zoom, NO pan, NO click handler, and NO 3x3 grid overlay — the brief's '3x3 grid' does not exist on this surface. The canvas only auto-rotates portrait/landscape via decideOrient for layout (DetectorImage.tsx:77-105) and applies a warm LUT; it is non-interactive. The q-link DetectorRingOverlay exists only on the Focus surface (FocusDetectorPanel.tsx:83), never on the loupe — so a user inspecting a pattern in the loupe cannot see or hover Bragg rings here.
interactions.recommendation: Decide intent: if the loupe is meant to be a 'screen the frame' surface, the inert static image is acceptable and the brief's grid/zoom expectation is simply not a feature. If deeper single-pattern inspection is wanted, consider zoom-on-scroll / click-to-zoom, or surface the ring overlay (already built) so ring inspection isn't gated behind entering Focus. At minimum, the static frame should not look interactive (no hover affordance currently, so this is honest).

interactions.location: absent (searched components/ + pages/; not present in Loupe surface)
interactions.detail: The brief lists 'Reprocess before indexing' as an expected loupe control; it does not exist on this surface. The closest analogue is the StaleIndicesBanner Re-analyze button (StaleIndicesBanner.tsx:73-76) which lives on the Focus/Index surface, not the loupe. There is no reprocess/reanalyze affordance in LoupePage/LoupeFrame/LoupeSidebar.
interactions.recommendation: If reprocessing-before-indexing is part of the intended loupe workflow, add it near the Representative section (reuse useReanalyzeExposure as StaleIndicesBanner does). Otherwise drop the expectation. Tie it to the missing 'Open in Focus' action so the natural sequence reads: pick rep -> (reprocess if needed) -> index.

interactions.detail: Reveals the inline key:value form (setEditing(true)). Routes through useAddCorpusSampleTag (queries.ts:579) — the same corpus mutator the contact sheet uses, so an add is visible on the sheet without refetch (per comment LoupeSidebar.tsx:72-74). Two render paths: a dashed '+ tag' pill when no tags exist (line 101) and a compact '+' button alongside existing chips (line 178).
interactions.recommendation: None.

interactions.element: Sample tag form — key input / value input / Add / cancel
interactions.detail: Value input: Enter=submit, Escape=reset, autoFocus (lines 151-155). submit() trims value, ignores empty value, fires add.mutate({key,value}) then resets (lines 89-96). Add button and cancel ✕ both work. The keyboard guard in LoupePage (tag===INPUT/TEXTAREA returns early, LoupePage.tsx:144-145) correctly prevents the global X/R/arrow shortcuts from firing while typing a tag.
interactions.recommendation: Minor: the key input has no Enter/Escape handler (only the value input does, line 151) — pressing Enter while focused in the key field does nothing. Add the same onKeyDown to the key input for consistency.

interactions.detail: aria-label 'Remove <key|value> tag'; onClick=remove.mutate(tag.id) via useRemoveCorpusSampleTag (queries.ts:587). Keyboard reachable as a real <button>.
interactions.recommendation: None.

interactions.detail: Display-only meter; level = active exposure's detected-peak count clamped 0..5 (LoupePage.tsx:100-101 usePeaks, SignalMeter clamps). Not interactive; correctly not presented as such. Honest proxy per its own doc comment.
interactions.recommendation: None (display-only by design).

interactions.detail: Both render a hardcoded '—' placeholder. The doc comment (lines 229-236) says they 'stub to — until the backend fields are plumbed'. A scientist reading 'integration / collected' expects real exposure facts (integration time, collection timestamp); they are permanently dashes today.
interactions.recommendation: Either plumb the backend fields and populate these, or hide the rows until data exists — two permanent em-dashes read as broken metadata rather than 'not yet available'.

interactions.element: Contact sheet | Loupe view switch (Loupe segment)
interactions.detail: On a loupe route the Loupe segment renders as a static active <span> (not a button) — correct, since you are already on it. The Contact-sheet segment is a Link to /samples (preserving ?beamtime=, lines 207-215) and works. Off a loupe route the Loupe segment is a disabled <button> with title 'Open a sample to use the loupe' (lines 226-234) — reasonable, since no sample is selected. The switch is route-derived, not sample-id aware.
interactions.recommendation: None. The disabled-with-tooltip state is an honest affordance. (Note the asymmetry: the Loupe's own Back link drops ?beamtime= while this topbar Link preserves it — see the Back finding.)

interactions.element: Index stage tab (topbar) as a route into indexing from loupe
interactions.detail: On a /samples/loupe route, onSampleRoute is false (pathname starts with /samples, not /sample/), so the Index tab's isActive is false and it renders disabled with cursor-not-allowed. It therefore cannot serve as the loupe->indexing bridge. Combined with the absent in-loupe 'Open in Focus' action, there is no topbar path into indexing from the loupe either.
interactions.recommendation: Covered by the 'Path from Loupe into Index/Focus' finding — the fix is an in-loupe action, since the topbar Index tab is intentionally inert without an active sample route.

interactions.detail: Documents ←/→ flip, X drop/restore, R set representative, Esc back. All four are wired in LoupePage's keydown handler (lines 142-154) and all function. The legend is accurate. Notably it does NOT list any 'index this sample' / 'go to Focus' key — consistent with that path being absent.
interactions.recommendation: When the loupe->Focus action is added, give it a key (e.g. Enter or I) and list it here.

frictionFindings: Back-to-sheet (link + Esc) drops the ?beamtime= filter, so a user who arrived from a filtered contact sheet returns to the unfiltered all-experiments sheet and must re-filter — CorpusTopbar's own sheet Link preserves beamtime, so this is an inconsistency, LoupePage.tsx:137 vs CorpusTopbar.tsx:196.

No in-flight feedback on the two primary queue mutations (Drop/Restore, Set representative): the buttons stay fully enabled while the mutation is pending, so the user gets no confirmation that the click registered until the cache flips, and a double-tap fires twice (absorbed by idempotency but visually mute), LoupeSidebar.tsx:274-321.

The filmstrip cells are clickable divs without tabIndex/role/keyboard handlers, so the strip is not tab-reachable (arrow keys flip frames but you cannot focus a specific thumb) — the contact-sheet thumb is a proper keyboard button, ThumbnailGallery.tsx:41-89.
'integration' and 'collected' meta rows are permanent em-dashes; reading as broken metadata rather than 'not yet available', LoupeSidebar.tsx:241-242.

The big detector frame offers no inspection interactions at all (no zoom, no ring overlay) even though the ring overlay is already built for Focus; deep single-pattern inspection is gated behind leaving the loupe, DetectorImage.tsx + FocusDetectorPanel.tsx:83.
The tag key input lacks Enter/Escape handling that the value input has, a small inconsistency in the inline tag form, LoupeSidebar.tsx:136-159.
deadEnds: The Loupe is a navigational dead-end with respect to the core workflow: there is no way to proceed from inspecting/picking a representative into the Index/Focus stage (/sample/:id). The only exit is 'Back to the sheet' (/samples). The sidebar explicitly tells the user the representative 'carries forward to the Index stage' yet provides no on-ramp to it; the topbar Index tab is disabled on loupe routes. The user must back out to the contact sheet and re-enter the sample by another route to index it — LoupePage.tsx:136-138, LoupeSidebar.tsx:311-321, CorpusTopbar.tsx:140-160.

Rename is unreachable from the loupe (and from anywhere in the UI): api.updateSample({display_name}) and useUpdateSample exist but are only ever called with {notes}; the loupe headline is static text — api.ts:125, queries.ts:523, FocusWorkspaceLayout.tsx:126.
'Reprocess before indexing' has no entry point on the loupe; the only reanalyze affordance lives on a different surface (StaleIndicesBanner on Focus) — StaleIndicesBanner.tsx:73-76.
notes:
The Loupe's local interactions are largely solid and correctly wired — switch exposure (click + arrows), Drop/Restore (button + X), Set representative (button + R), tag add/remove (full inline CRUD through the shared corpus mutator), Back (button + Esc). The keyboard legend is honest and complete for what exists. The real problems are at the seams of the workflow, not in the widgets:

1. HEADLINE ISSUE — the inspect->index loop does not close. After a scientist screens frames, drops bad ones, and picks the representative, the loupe gives them nowhere to GO. There is literally no link into /sample/:id (Focus/Index). This is the single highest-value fix: add an 'Open in Focus' / 'Index this sample' action (likely in the Representative section, enabled once a rep exists), and give it a key.

2. Rename is an expected-but-absent affordance even though the backend mutator is fully built and wired for notes — the loupe headline should be the inline-rename entry point.

3. 'Reprocess before indexing' and the '3x3 grid'/zoom from the brief do not exist on this surface at all; treat as deliberate scoping decisions or genuine gaps depending on product intent.

4. Two smaller IA inconsistencies worth fixing cheaply: Back drops ?beamtime= (CorpusTopbar preserves it), and the filmstrip cells aren't keyboard-focusable (contact-sheet thumbs are). Neither blocks the workflow but both add friction.

Verified by reading: LoupePage.tsx, LoupeFrame.tsx, LoupeSidebar.tsx, DetectorImage.tsx, ThumbnailGallery.tsx, RejectXMark.tsx, CorpusTopbar.tsx, ContactSheetRow.tsx (loupe-open path), and grepping queries.ts/api.ts for the rename/representative/reanalyze mutators and AppRoutes.tsx for the route map. The detector frame has no click/zoom/grid handlers and DetectorRingOverlay is referenced only by FocusDetectorPanel, never the loupe."

interactions.detail: onClick navigates to /series/new, which AppRoutes.tsx:97 maps to SeriesScopingPage (a real confirm-and-build picker). Keyboard reachable (native button). The accent-filled styling makes it the clear primary action.
interactions.recommendation: Keep. This is the genuine series-creation entry point.

interactions.detail: Controlled input → setSearch → filterSort (folioFilter.ts:33-36) filters case-insensitively on s.title.includes(needle) only. type=search gives a native clear affordance. Filtering is real but title-only: it does NOT match the ordering variable, author, member phase names, or description even though SeriesSummary carries description/author_username/member_phases. A scientist searching 'Pn3m' or a lipid name they remember from the series content will get an empty 'No series match' even when matching cards exist.
interactions.recommendation: Widen the needle match in filterSort to also include description, author_username, and member_phases (all already on SeriesSummary). Title-only search is a hidden, narrower-than-expected scope.

interactions.detail: setFilter('all'); filterSort applies no filter branch. aria-pressed reflects state; active = ink fill. Default state.
interactions.recommendation: Keep.

interactions.detail: setFilter('transition'); filterSort keeps rows where s.member_phase_count > 1. This is a real, data-backed filter (member_phase_count comes from the backend listing).
interactions.recommendation: Keep. Note the semantics are 'spans >1 distinct phase' (an approximation of 'has transition'), which is acceptable but could mis-include a series with two phases that aren't a monotonic transition; document only.

interactions.detail: setFilter('cross') is wired and the chip toggles aria-pressed, BUT filterSort unconditionally sets rows = [] for this filter (folioFilter.ts:42-43) because there is no sample→experiment join on the SeriesSummary listing. Result: clicking it ALWAYS empties the grid and shows the 'No series match' empty state regardless of corpus content. The control looks selectable and live but can never produce a non-empty result — a guaranteed dead end on every click. The module comment acknowledges it is data-starved.
interactions.recommendation: Do not ship a chip that always returns zero. Either (a) compute the cross-experiment signal on the backend listing (add a boolean like spans_multiple_experiments to SeriesSummary) and wire the real filter, or (b) hide/remove the chip until that signal exists. A control that universally produces an empty state is worse than absent — it teaches the user the folio is broken.

interactions.detail: setSort('recent'); filterSort preserves backend order (last_event_at DESC). aria-pressed + ink-fill on active. Default.
interactions.recommendation: Keep.

interactions.detail: Labelled 'Variable' but filterSort sorts by a.title.localeCompare(b.title) — it sorts alphabetically by title, NOT by the ordering variable. The listing SeriesSummary does not carry ordering_variable (only the per-series detail does, see SeriesFolioCard.tsx:71 useSeries). So this segment lies about what it does: a scientist choosing 'Variable' expecting temperature/concentration grouping gets an A-Z title sort instead. The mislabel is documented in folioFilter.ts:11-14 but is invisible to the user.
interactions.recommendation: Either surface ordering_variable on the SeriesSummary listing (backend) and sort by it for real, or relabel the segment 'Title' (A-Z) so the control tells the truth. A sort whose label contradicts its behaviour erodes trust in every other control.

interactions.detail: setSort('size'); filterSort sorts by b.member_count - a.member_count (descending). Real, data-backed.
interactions.recommendation: Keep.

interactions.detail: The entire card is a single <button>; onClick → onOpen(series.id) → navigate(`/series/${id}`) → SeriesBuilderPage (AppRoutes.tsx:99). Clicking ANYWHERE on the card — mini-waterfall, phase strip, title, meta line, footer — opens the builder, since they are all children of the one button with no nested handlers. Keyboard reachable; hover lift gives feedback. This is the right low-friction model (one click from folio to builder).
interactions.recommendation: Keep the whole-card target. See sub-element notes below for affordances a user might expect to be independently clickable but are not.

interactions.detail: Pure read-only SVG (no event handlers of its own). It is NOT independently interactive — clicking it bubbles to the parent card button and opens the builder. This is deliberate (the doc comment calls it the 'read-only geometry variant', not MultiTracePlot). A user might expect hover-to-inspect a trace, but that lives in the builder. Acceptable: the affordance is 'open this series', not 'inspect this trace'.
interactions.recommendation: Keep read-only. No per-trace tooltip needed at folio density.

interactions.detail: Read-only colored segments + transition caption; no handlers, clicks bubble to the card button. A scientist scanning the wall for a specific phase transition (e.g. Pn3m→Lamellar) cannot click a segment to filter/jump — but the 'Has transition' chip partially covers this intent. Segments have no title/tooltip, so the phase name of a segment is only legible via the caption (first→last); intermediate members' phases are not surfaced on hover.
interactions.recommendation: Optional low-cost win: add a title attribute per ps-seg (the member's phase + sample label) so hovering a segment reveals which sample/phase it is, without making it a separate click target.

interactions.detail: A terracotta dot appears when series.has_stale_members. It carries a title='Has stale members' tooltip but no dedicated action — clicking it just opens the series (bubbles to card). A scientist seeing 'stale' would reasonably expect a one-click 'reanalyze' or jump-to-stale affordance; instead they must open the builder and hunt. The dot is informational only.
interactions.recommendation: Acceptable as an indicator, but consider making the stale state actionable from the folio (e.g. a small 'reconcile' link in the card footer) so the user doesn't have to open every flagged series to find the stale member. At minimum the tooltip is good; keep it.

interactions.detail: The pill is fully wired but newMatches defaults to 0 and the folio page (SeriesFolioPage.tsx:174-181) never passes a newMatches prop, so it renders for NO card on the current corpus. The prop doc (SeriesFolioCard.tsx:13-19) confirms there is no recipe-match data source yet. It is also non-interactive even when shown (clicking bubbles to open the series). So today it is invisible dead code; tomorrow, if lit, it would still be a non-actionable label where a user would expect 'click to add the N matching samples'.
interactions.recommendation: Lower priority since it never renders. When a recipe-match source lands, wire the pill to a real action (add-matching-members) rather than shipping it as a passive label — otherwise it advertises N new matches with no way to act on them.

interactions.detail: Non-interactive display. Shows visible.length and switches its sublabel to 'of {total} shown' when isFiltered. Correctly reflects filter/search state. Good ambient feedback.
interactions.recommendation: Keep.

interactions.detail: When series.length === 0 the page shows plain text 'No series yet. Select samples on the contact sheet to start one.' This copy points at a DIFFERENT flow than the page's own primary CTA: the header '+ New series' button goes to /series/new (the scoping picker), while the empty-state text tells the user to go to the contact sheet. Neither the contact sheet link NOR the New-series button is present inside the empty block — it is inert text. A first-time user on an empty folio has no in-context click to act; they must visually re-find the header CTA (still rendered above) or navigate away to the contact sheet themselves.
interactions.recommendation: Put an actionable button in the empty state. interactions.detail: Renders as a dropdown (rounded border, bg-plate, a ▾ chevron at line 21) — every visual cue of a selectable control — but it is a static div with no onClick, no handler, no options. The component doc (line 6-9) admits it: 'Read-only in this milestone — re-selecting the ordering variable is a follow-up; the field still presents as a decision.' The caret is aria-hidden so screen readers won't announce it as interactive, but sighted users will click it and nothing happens. This is described as 'the one real decision on this surface' yet it cannot be exercised.
interactions.recommendation: Either wire it to a real picker over the corpus tag keys (proposeOrdering already computes the freq map; surfacing the runner-up keys is cheap) or remove the ▾ chevron and dropdown styling so it doesn't promise an interaction it won't deliver. interactions.element: Drag grip (⠿) on each member row
interactions.detail: Styled cursor-grab + select-none with the braille drag glyph ⠿, the universal 'drag to reorder' affordance. But there is NO drag handler: grep for draggable/onDrag/onDrop/dnd across Scoping*.tsx and SeriesScopingPage.tsx finds nothing. aria-hidden, not keyboard reachable. Ordering is computed purely by parseSortKey (SeriesScopingPage.tsx:111-119) and the comment at :110 states it 'does NOT reorder the batch payload.' So the grip suggests manual reordering that does not exist, and even the sort it implies has no payload effect.
interactions.recommendation: Remove the grip (the order is machine-derived and immutable here), OR implement drag reorder. Showing a grab handle that cannot be grabbed is pure friction — the scientist will try to drag a mis-ordered sample and fail silently.

interactions.detail: Click on a non-flagged value re-opens it as a text input (open() → setEditing(true)). Good: every value stays re-editable, including ones resolved by mistake. Keyboard reachable (it's a <button>). Hover shows a dotted underline cue. Title 'Click to re-open this value'.
interactions.recommendation: None. This is a well-designed confirm-not-fill-out affordance.

interactions.element: Value cell — flagged state ('▸ check the read')
interactions.detail: Click on a flagged value calls onToggleFlag() (NOT an edit) — 'accept the read in one click' (line 27). So one click clears the flag and accepts the empty/parsed value. This is subtle: a flagged row usually has value==='' (proposeOrdering sets flagged=value===''), so 'accepting the read' confirms a BLANK value. The affordance to actually TYPE a value on a flagged row is non-obvious: you accept (clears flag) and only then can click again to edit.
interactions.recommendation: For a flagged (missing-value) row the primary need is to TYPE the value, not 'accept' a blank. Consider: flagged click opens the input directly (so the scientist enters the value in one step), and provide a separate explicit 'accept blank' affordance only if that's a real use case. Also guard the build gate against accepted-but-empty values (changeValue sets flagged=value==="" at :177, but toggleFlag at :179-183 can clear the flag on an empty value, letting an empty tag through).

interactions.detail: autoFocus, commits on blur and Enter, cancels on Escape restoring prior value. changeValue (SeriesScopingPage.tsx:174-178) snapshots for undo and re-derives flagged=value===''. Clean.
interactions.recommendation: None.

interactions.element: '+ Add to series' on a loose match
interactions.detail: Moves a loose-match sample into rows with include:true and removes it from loose, snapshotting for undo. Works. BUT: loose matches by definition lack a value for the ordering key (the section explains 'No value for the ordering variable — add it to include'). addLoose adds the row but does NOT prompt for the value, and the moved row keeps its original value (likely '' → flagged). So 'Add to series' immediately produces a flagged row that blocks the build gate, with no inline path to supply the value at the moment of adding.
interactions.recommendation: On add, either open the value input inline so the scientist supplies the missing ordering value in the same gesture, or scroll/focus the newly added (now-flagged) row. Otherwise adding a loose match silently re-blocks the build gate and the user must hunt for the new flagged row.

interactions.detail: Toggles expanded=true to reveal loose matches beyond COLLAPSED_COUNT=4. One-way (no 'show less'). Keyboard reachable. interactions.detail: Pops the in-session history stack restoring rows+loose. Button only renders when history.length>0. Cmd/Ctrl-Z bound globally with preventDefault. Title shows the last action label. Works and is discoverable. One gap: no redo.

Surface verified against live source. CRITICAL CORRECTION FOR ORCHESTRATOR: the brief listed components/SamplePickerRow.tsx as a scoping-surface file, but it is NOT used on /series/new. It is a Compare-page picker component (components/AGENTS.md:11 lists it under Compare; grep finds zero importers in app source — only test/SamplePickerRow.test.tsx). The actual scoping surface composes ScopingAutogroupCard, ScopingOrderField, ScopingRow (+ ScopingValueCell, ScopingSparkline), ScopingLooseMatches, ScopingPhaseStrip, ScopingFoot, ScopingConfirmModal. I audited those and additionally documented SamplePickerRow's disabled branch since the brief asked.

ROOT-CAUSE THEME: the surface is built as a 'machine-proposes / human-confirms' worksheet (good model) but it is decoupled from selection. The whole-corpus read + 'You selected N samples' copy + the admission in ScopingLooseMatches.tsx:15-18 ('no contact-sheet selection plumbing yet') point to ONE missing piece: a selection hand-off from the contact sheet into /series/new. Wiring that would simultaneously fix the misleading autogroup copy, the missing contact-sheet entry point, the over-long loose-match list, and the cold-corpus dead end (you'd arrive with samples + tags in hand).

MOST INERT AFFORDANCES (highest 'looks interactive, isn't' cost): (1) 'Ordered by' dropdown, (2) drag grip, (3) cold-corpus empty-state instruction with no door. These three should be the top of the remediation list.

POTENTIAL DATA BUG worth a second look: toggleFlag (SeriesScopingPage.tsx:179-183) flips flagged without regard to value, while changeValue (:174-178) ties flagged to value===''. The flagged value cell's 'accept the read' path (ScopingValueCell.tsx:27) therefore can clear a flag on an empty value, and canBuild (:168-172) only checks !flagged — so an accepted-but-empty ordering value can pass the gate and be written as an empty-string scoping tag. Verify whether the backend rejects empty tag values; if not, this is a wiring-bug, not just friction.

The Confirm & build gate itself (footer disabled-state + tooltip + state line) is the model for how disabled controls SHOULD explain themselves on this surface — reuse that pattern when fixing the silent SamplePickerRow grey-out."

Verified against live source. Mount topology: App.tsx mounts AppRoutes + OnboardingFlow + NavModal + InfrastructureBanner + ToastContainer + SeriesCommitConflictModal app-wide; CorpusShell (the layout route) renders CorpusTopbar + <Outlet/>. StaleIndicesBanner is mounted inside PhasePanel (focus surface), included here per task scope.

Root cause of the central defect: the corpus shell was deliberately built URL-first (useSyncActiveSampleFromRoute is intentionally one-way to avoid a store→URL resolving handshake), but the NavModal and the '/' / ⌘K shortcuts were carried over from the retired store-driven Index workspace and never re-pointed at the router. The fix is small (add useNavigate to NavModal.commitSample) and would convert the picker from dead-end back to the app's fastest intent→result path — directly serving the 'minimize clicks between intent and result' goal.

Severity ranking for this surface: (1) NavModal sample-commit wiring-bug — fix first; (2) Index tab affordance — make navigable or remove; (3) Beamtime chip no-op on /series + /sample and lost on stage switch; (4) stale onboarding copy; (5) dead TitleButton / missing visible picker entry point; (6) non-clickable wordmark. Items 2–6 are low-effort and reduce friction without any IA change.

Two correctly-modeled patterns worth preserving as references: the disabled Loupe segment with an explanatory title tooltip (CorpusTopbar.tsx:226-235) and the StaleIndicesBanner's self-clearing pending-aware Re-analyze button — both are the right way to handle a temporarily-unavailable action; the Index tab and Beamtime chip should imitate the former."
